h: Building an Island Day Around the Rainforest
p: Arreton sits slap in the middle of the Isle of Wight, and that central spot is a real bonus. Nowhere on the island is a long drive away, so the zoo slots easily into a holiday whether you're staying in Shanklin, Ryde, Ventnor or out west near Freshwater.

Right on the doorstep is Arreton Barns, a cluster of old farm buildings with craft shops, a pub and plenty of history about rural island life, which makes a handy lunch stop. Robin Hill, the woodland adventure park with toboggan runs and treetop trails, is only a few minutes up the road too, so active kids can run off whatever energy the sloths didn't use up. Head down to Sandown and Dinosaur Isle shows off fossils dug from the island's own cliffs; the Isle of Wight is one of the best places in Europe for dinosaur remains, and the kids won't believe the bones came from a beach near their caravan.

A few tips. Bring a camera that copes with low light, as the tropical houses are warm and dim and the animals like to hide. Allow a couple of hours to go round properly. And if you've arrived as foot passengers on the ferry, the island's buses cover Arreton, so a car isn't essential.
